findings.claim: ServletExchange.abort() is deliberately lock-free and calls AsyncContext.complete() from stop()/completeAll() or an AsyncListener thread while an SSE drain thread may be inside FlushingStream.write/flush on the same response. The Servlet spec leaves a response write that races complete() undefined; a container that recycles request/response objects on complete (Tomcat-style) could see the drain write on a recycled response. The 'aborted before complete' ordering guards only later writes, not one already in progress. Only Jetty 9.4 is verified and docs/api/servlet.md says so, so no defect is observed today; later waves that add a container (Tomcat/WildFly) will hit it.
findings.evidence: NaruServe-servlet/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/servlet/ServletExchange.java:196-201 (abort -> complete), NaruServe-servlet/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/servlet/ServletEventStream.java:171-180 (completeAll) and 215-231 (writes under synchronized(ex) that abort() does not take)
findings.suggested_fix: If a non-Jetty container is ever verified, complete the AsyncContext from the drain thread (it already completes in drainTask's finally) and let completeAll only set aborted plus a write timeout, or take the exchange lock with a bounded tryLock before complete(). Until then keep the Jetty-only statement in docs/api/servlet.md.

findings.claim: A file input left empty in a browser form arrives as a part with filename="" and an empty body. MultipartParser.params() keeps the empty quoted value, so p.get("filename") is "" (not null), the part is spooled as a file part, and FormData.firstFile/files treat it as a file because they test only filename() != null. req.file("avatar") therefore returns a zero-byte UploadFile with filename "" instead of null, so the documented guard in the multipart.md example (if file == null -> 400 Missing file) never fires for a browser form, and file.save(dest) writes an empty file. multer (the Express counterpart the doc maps to) drops such a part. The behaviour is neither documented nor pinned by a test (no test or doc mentions an empty filename).
findings.evidence: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/MultipartParser.java:96 (filename != null branch) and params() keeps v="" for filename=""; NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/FormData.java:91 and :103 (filename() != null); docs/api/multipart.md:21 (file == null guard in the example)
findings.suggested_fix: Either treat an empty filename with an empty body as an absent file (skip the part, still count it in maxParts) so req.file returns null, or state in docs/api/multipart.md that a browser sends filename="" for an empty file input and that handlers must check file.filename().isEmpty() / file.size() == 0; add a test with filename="" in either case.

findings.claim: HttpExchange.sendFile has two different check orders in the two shipped adapters and the SPI Javadoc fixes neither. TinyHttpdExchange.sendFile validates the range first (IllegalArgumentException) and then the abort/single-start rule, while ServletExchange.sendFile runs requireStartable() first and the range after. On an already started or aborted exchange with a bad range, Tiny throws IllegalArgumentException and Servlet throws IllegalStateException/IOException. The Tiny inline comment ('the abort check and single-start rule win over a failed open') also contradicts its own order for the range check. The core never calls sendFile (DefaultResponse.sendBody streams through commit), so no user path is affected today; the SPI contract test only covers the happy range.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one order (start/abort rule first, as the Servlet adapter and the Tiny comment say), apply it in TinyHttpdExchange.sendFile, state it in the HttpExchange.sendFile Javadoc and add a shared SPI contract case for a bad range on a started exchange.
